purpose: Teach: 従兄弟/見分け/嫌っ/よくなる/こらえ/探さ/さして/ペンキ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんの、本気で、絶対、従兄弟、絶対、よく集まったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, when you were young — do you remember how often Dad and my cousins would gather together?
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Slight lean forward. The rhythm of someone retrieving an old memory, voice warm with the weight of years. Gentle searching in the phrasing.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、お顔の、絶対、見分け、絶対、お得意だったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Mm. When you were young, your grandfather — he had such a gift for telling the family apart by their faces. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Warm reminiscence, voice brightening with the recollection. A small, genuine smile in the delivery. Unhurried, almost savoring the detail. The cadence of someone sharing a beloved family trait.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、嫌っ、絶対、てた、絶対、お料理、絶対、克服されたわよな、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, Gran — you really didn't enjoy cooking at first, but you learned to love it, didn't you?
lines.style: Quieter, more reflective. A note of admiration underneath. The slight hesitation before 'love' — acknowledging the journey it took. Voice trailing gently, as if seeing her through younger eyes.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、お父さんの、本気で、絶対、お加減、絶対、よくなる、絶対、よう、絶対、お祈りされたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, your grandfather — he used to pray so often that your father's health would improve. You remember those days, don't you?
lines.style: Voice softens with the memory of devotion. A tender pause before 'pray' — the solemnity of it. Unhurried phrasing that honors the tenderness of that time. Eyes distant, present but far away.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、辛い時、絶対、こらえ、絶対、てくれたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, Gran — through the hard times, you just kept going. You bore it all for us. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Quiet but firm with conviction. A slight catch before 'hard times' — the weight of what it cost. Slow tempo, each phrase deliberate. Voice steady with gratitude and the ache of understanding what she endured.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、お仕事、絶対、探さ、絶対、れた、絶対、時期、絶対、ありましたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, your grandfather — there was that period when he was searching for work. Those days were there too, weren't they?
lines.style: Gentle acknowledgment of difficulty without dwelling. Voice even, measured. A slight softening at the edges — not shying from the truth, but holding it tenderly. The rhythm of someone being honest about what was real.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、さして、絶対、文句、絶対、おっしゃらなかったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, Gran — you didn't complain, not really. Not even when you might have had every reason to.
lines.style: Voice fills with quiet reverence. A long, slight pause before the final phrase — letting the weight of her dignity settle in the air. Slow delivery, each word carefully placed. The tone of someone finally naming something they've always known.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、お家の、絶対、ペンキ、絶対、お塗りになったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, your grandfather — he painted the house himself, didn't he? I still remember that.
lines.style: Voice brightens slightly, almost tender-close. A small warmth in recalling the image of him with brush in hand. Gentle rhythm, the ease of remembering something concrete and real. Nearness in the delivery — sharing the memory together.
